Washington (state).title: Washington (state)
Washington (state).extract: Washington is a state in the Pacific Northwest region of the United States. It is often referred to as Washington state to distinguish it from the national capital; both are named after George Washington, a U.S. Founding Father and the first U.S. president.

Adams County, Washington.title: Adams County, Washington
Adams County, Washington.extract: Adams County is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 20,613.

Asotin County, Washington.title: Asotin County, Washington
Asotin County, Washington.extract: Asotin County () is a county in the far southeastern corner of the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 22,285.

Benton County, Washington.title: Benton County, Washington
Benton County, Washington.extract: Benton County is a county in the south-central portion of the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 206,873.

Chelan County, Washington.title: Chelan County, Washington
Chelan County, Washington.extract: Chelan County (, shə-LAN) is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 79,074.

Clallam County, Washington.title: Clallam County, Washington
Clallam County, Washington.extract: Clallam County is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 77,155, with an estimated population of 77,616 in 2023.

Clark County, Washington.title: Clark County, Washington
Clark County, Washington.extract: Clark County is the southernmost county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 503,311, making it Washington's fifth-most populous county.

Columbia County, Washington.title: Columbia County, Washington
Columbia County, Washington.extract: Columbia County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 3,952, making it the second-least populous county in Washington.

Cowlitz County, Washington.title: Cowlitz County, Washington
Cowlitz County, Washington.extract: Cowlitz County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 110,730.

Douglas County, Washington.title: Douglas County, Washington
Douglas County, Washington.extract: Douglas County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 42,938.

Ferry County, Washington.title: Ferry County, Washington
Ferry County, Washington.extract: Ferry County is a county located on the northern border of the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 7,178, making it the fourth-least populous county in Washington.

Franklin County, Washington.title: Franklin County, Washington
Franklin County, Washington.extract: Franklin County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 96,749, and was estimated to be 102,612 in 2025.

Garfield County, Washington.title: Garfield County, Washington
Garfield County, Washington.extract: Garfield County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 2,286, making it the least populous county in Washington; with about 3.2 inhabitants per square mile (1.2/km2), it is also the least densely populated county in Washington.

Grant County, Washington.title: Grant County, Washington
Grant County, Washington.extract: Grant County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 99,123.

Grays Harbor County, Washington.title: Grays Harbor County, Washington
Grays Harbor County, Washington.extract: Grays Harbor County is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 75,636.

Island County, Washington.title: Island County, Washington
Island County, Washington.extract: Island County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 86,857.

Jefferson County, Washington.title: Jefferson County, Washington
Jefferson County, Washington.extract: Jefferson County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 32,977.

King County, Washington.title: King County, Washington
King County, Washington.extract: King County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. The population was 2,269,675 in the 2020 census, making it the most populous county in Washington, and the 13th-most populous in the United States.

Kitsap County, Washington.title: Kitsap County, Washington
Kitsap County, Washington.extract: Kitsap County is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 275,611.

Kittitas County, Washington.title: Kittitas County, Washington
Kittitas County, Washington.extract: Kittitas County () is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. At the 2020 census, its population was 44,337.

Klickitat County, Washington.title: Klickitat County, Washington
Klickitat County, Washington.extract: Klickitat County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 22,735.

Lewis County, Washington.title: Lewis County, Washington
Lewis County, Washington.extract: Lewis County is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the county's population was 82,149.

Lincoln County, Washington.title: Lincoln County, Washington
Lincoln County, Washington.extract: Lincoln County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 10,876, making it the fifth-least populous county in the state.

Mason County, Washington.title: Mason County, Washington
Mason County, Washington.extract: Mason County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 65,726.

Okanogan County, Washington.title: Okanogan County, Washington
Okanogan County, Washington.extract: Okanogan County () is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington along the Canada–U.S. border. As of the 2020 census, the population was 42,104.

Pacific County, Washington.title: Pacific County, Washington
Pacific County, Washington.extract: Pacific County is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 23,365.

Pierce County, Washington.title: Pierce County, Washington
Pierce County, Washington.extract: Pierce County is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 921,130, and was estimated to be 946,288 in 2025, making it the second-most populous county in Washington, behind King County, and the 60th-most populous in the United States.

Pend Oreille County, Washington.title: Pend Oreille County, Washington
Pend Oreille County, Washington.extract: Pend Oreille County ( POND-ə-RAY) is a county located in the northeast corner of the U.S. state of Washington, along the Canada–US border. As of the 2020 census, the population was 13,401.

San Juan County, Washington.title: San Juan County, Washington
San Juan County, Washington.extract: San Juan County is a county in the Salish Sea in the far northwestern corner of the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 17,788.

Skagit County, Washington.title: Skagit County, Washington
Skagit County, Washington.extract: Skagit County is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 129,523.

Skamania County, Washington.title: Skamania County, Washington
Skamania County, Washington.extract: Skamania County ( skə-MAY-nee-ə) is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 12,036.

Snohomish County, Washington.title: Snohomish County, Washington
Snohomish County, Washington.extract: Snohomish County () is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. With a population of 827,957 as of the 2020 census, it is the third-most populous county in Washington, after nearby King and Pierce counties, and the 72nd-most populous in the United States.

Spokane County, Washington.title: Spokane County, Washington
Spokane County, Washington.extract: Spokane County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 539,339, and was estimated to be 555,947 in 2024, making it the fourth-most populous county in Washington.

Stevens County, Washington.title: Stevens County, Washington
Stevens County, Washington.extract: Stevens County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington along the Canada–US border. At the 2020 census, its population was 46,445.

Thurston County, Washington.title: Thurston County, Washington
Thurston County, Washington.extract: Thurston County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 294,793.

Wahkiakum County, Washington.title: Wahkiakum County, Washington
Wahkiakum County, Washington.extract: Wahkiakum County ( wə-KY-ə-kum) is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 4,422, making it the third-least populous county in Washington.

Walla Walla County, Washington.title: Walla Walla County, Washington
Walla Walla County, Washington.extract: Walla Walla County ( WAH-lə WAH-lə) is a county located in the southeast of the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 62,584.

Whatcom County, Washington.title: Whatcom County, Washington
Whatcom County, Washington.extract: Whatcom County (, ) is a county located in the northwestern corner of the U.S. state of Washington, bordered by the Lower Mainland (the Metro Vancouver and Fraser Valley Regional Districts) of the Canadian province of British Columbia to the north, Okanogan County to the east, Skagit County to the south, San Juan…

Whitman County, Washington.title: Whitman County, Washington
Whitman County, Washington.extract: Whitman County is a county located in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, the population was 47,973.

Yakima County, Washington.title: Yakima County, Washington
Yakima County, Washington.extract: Yakima County is a county in the U.S. state of Washington. As of the 2020 census, its population was 256,728.

Aberdeen, Washington.title: Aberdeen, Washington
Aberdeen, Washington.extract: Aberdeen ( AB-ər-deen) is a city in Grays Harbor County, Washington, United States. The population was 17,013 at the 2020 census.

Airway Heights, Washington.title: Airway Heights, Washington
Airway Heights, Washington.extract: Airway Heights is a city in Spokane County, Washington, United States, just west of Spokane. It is part of the Spokane metropolitan area and had a population of 10,757 at the 2020 census, and was estimated at 11,950 in 2024.

Albion, Washington.title: Albion, Washington
Albion, Washington.extract: Albion is a town in Whitman County, Washington, United States. The population was 550 at the 2020 Census.

Algona, Washington.title: Algona, Washington
Algona, Washington.extract: Algona () is a city in King County, Washington, United States, and the Seattle metropolitan area, surrounded by the suburbs of Auburn to the north and east, Pacific to the south, and unincorporated King County to the west. The population was 3,290 at the 2020 census, and was estimated at 3,269 in 2024.

Almira, Washington.title: Almira, Washington
Almira, Washington.extract: Almira () is a town in Lincoln County, Washington, United States. The population was 318 at the 2020 census.

Anacortes, Washington.title: Anacortes, Washington
Anacortes, Washington.extract: Anacortes ( AN-ə-KOR-təs) is a city in Skagit County, Washington, United States. The name "Anacortes" is an adaptation of the name of Anne Curtis Bowman, who was the wife of early Fidalgo Island settler Amos Bowman.

Arlington, Washington.title: Arlington, Washington
Arlington, Washington.extract: Arlington is a city in northern Snohomish County, Washington, United States, part of the Seattle metropolitan area. The city lies on the Stillaguamish River in the western foothills of the Cascade Range, adjacent to the city of Marysville.

Asotin, Washington.title: Asotin, Washington
Asotin, Washington.extract: Asotin ( ə-SOH-tən) is a city in and the county seat of Asotin County, Washington, United States. The population of the city was 1,204 at the 2020 census.

Auburn, Washington.title: Auburn, Washington
Auburn, Washington.extract: Auburn (Lushootseed: sladə) is a city in King County, Washington, United States (with a small portion crossing into neighboring Pierce County). The population was 87,256 at the 2020 Census, and was estimated at 85,513 in 2024.

Bainbridge Island, Washington.title: Bainbridge Island, Washington
Bainbridge Island, Washington.extract: Bainbridge Island is a city and island in Kitsap County, Washington, United States. It is located in Puget Sound.

Battle Ground, Washington.title: Battle Ground, Washington
Battle Ground, Washington.extract: Battle Ground is a city in Clark County, Washington, United States. The population was 20,743 at the 2020 census.

Beaux Arts Village, Washington.title: Beaux Arts Village, Washington
Beaux Arts Village, Washington.extract: Beaux Arts Village () is a town located in the Eastside region of King County, Washington, United States. It has a population of 317 as of the 2020 census and a land area of 0.1 sq mi.

Bellevue, Washington.title: Bellevue, Washington
Bellevue, Washington.extract: Bellevue (, BEL-vew) is a city in the Eastside region of King County, Washington, United States, located across Lake Washington from Seattle. It is the third-largest city in the Seattle metropolitan area, and the fifth-largest city in Washington.

Bellingham, Washington.title: Bellingham, Washington
Bellingham, Washington.extract: Bellingham ( BEL-ing-ham) is a city in and the county seat of Whatcom County in the U.S. state of Washington. It lies 21 miles (34 km) south of the Canada–United States border, between Vancouver, British Columbia, 52 miles (84 km) to the northwest and Seattle 90 miles (140 km) to the south.

Benton City, Washington.title: Benton City, Washington
Benton City, Washington.extract: Benton City is a city in Benton County, Washington, United States. It is also included in the Tri-Cities metropolitan area, which consists of both Benton and Franklin counties.

Bingen, Washington.title: Bingen, Washington
Bingen, Washington.extract: Bingen is a city in Klickitat County, Washington, United States. The population was 778 at the 2020 census.

Black Diamond, Washington.title: Black Diamond, Washington
Black Diamond, Washington.extract: Black Diamond is a city in King County, Washington, United States. The population was 4,697 at the 2020 census.

Blaine, Washington.title: Blaine, Washington
Blaine, Washington.extract: Blaine is a city in Whatcom County, Washington, United States. The city's northern boundary is the Canada–U.S. border; the Peace Arch international monument straddles the border of both countries.
Blaine, Washington.description: Border city in Washington, United States

Blue Ridge, Seattle.title: Blue Ridge, Seattle
Blue Ridge, Seattle.extract: North Beach / Blue Ridge is a neighborhood in the city of Seattle, in the U.S. state of Washington. The neighborhood is bounded on the south by Northwest 100th Street, beyond which lies Crown Hill; on the east by 12th Ave NW, beyond which lies Greenwood; on the north by Carkeek Park; and on the west by Puget Sound.

Bonney Lake, Washington.title: Bonney Lake, Washington
Bonney Lake, Washington.extract: Bonney Lake is a very busy city in Pierce County, Washington named for William P. Bonney. The population was 22,487 at the time of the 2020 census.

Bothell, Washington.title: Bothell, Washington
Bothell, Washington.extract: Bothell () is a city in King and Snohomish counties in the U.S. state of Washington. It is part of the Seattle metropolitan area, situated near the northeast end of Lake Washington in the Eastside region.

Bremerton, Washington.title: Bremerton, Washington
Bremerton, Washington.extract: Bremerton is a city in Kitsap County, Washington, United States. The population was 43,505 at the 2020 census and an estimated 44,122 in 2021, making it the largest city on the Kitsap Peninsula.

Brewster, Washington.title: Brewster, Washington
Brewster, Washington.extract: Brewster is a city in Okanogan County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,983 at the 2020 census.

Bridgeport, Washington.title: Bridgeport, Washington
Bridgeport, Washington.extract: Bridgeport is a city in Douglas County, Washington. It is part of the Wenatchee−East Wenatchee Metropolitan Statistical Area.

Brier, Washington.title: Brier, Washington
Brier, Washington.extract: Brier is a city in Snohomish County, Washington, United States. It is bordered by Mountlake Terrace to the west, Lynnwood to the north, Bothell to the east, and Lake Forest Park to the south.

Buckley, Washington.title: Buckley, Washington
Buckley, Washington.extract: Buckley is a city in Pierce County, Washington, United States, founded in 1882. The population was 5,114 at the 2020 census.

Bucoda, Washington.title: Bucoda, Washington
Bucoda, Washington.extract: Bucoda () is a town in Thurston County, Washington, United States. The population was 600 at the 2020 census.

Burien, Washington.title: Burien, Washington
Burien, Washington.extract: Burien ( BURE-ee-ən) is a suburban city in King County, Washington, United States, located south of Seattle on Puget Sound. As of the 2020 census, Burien's population was 52,066, which is a 56.3% increase since incorporation in 1993, making it the 25th most populous city in Washington.

Burlington, Washington.title: Burlington, Washington
Burlington, Washington.extract: Burlington is a city in Skagit County, Washington, United States. Its population was recorded as 9,152 in the 2020 census.

Camas, Washington.title: Camas, Washington
Camas, Washington.extract: Camas is a city in Clark County, Washington, with a population of 26,065 at the 2020 census. The east side of town borders the city of Washougal, Washington, and the west side of town borders Vancouver, Washington.

Carbonado, Washington.title: Carbonado, Washington
Carbonado, Washington.extract: Carbonado () is a town in Pierce County, Washington, United States. It is located near the Carbon River in the north of the county, approximately 50 miles (80 km) southeast of Seattle.

Carnation, Washington.title: Carnation, Washington
Carnation, Washington.extract: Carnation (Lushootseed: tultxʷ) is a city in King County, Washington, United States. It was historically known as Tolt and lies at the confluence of the Snoqualmie and Tolt rivers.

Cashmere, Washington.title: Cashmere, Washington
Cashmere, Washington.extract: Cashmere is a city in Chelan County, Washington, United States. It is part of the Wenatchee–East Wenatchee Metropolitan Statistical Area.

Castle Rock, Washington.title: Castle Rock, Washington
Castle Rock, Washington.extract: Castle Rock is a city in Cowlitz County, Washington, United States. Located between the Willapa Hills and the western base of Mount St. Helens, Castle Rock is at the heart of Washington timber country in the Pacific temperate rain forest.

Cathlamet, Washington.title: Cathlamet, Washington
Cathlamet, Washington.extract: Cathlamet is a town located along the Ocean Beach Highway in Wahkiakum County, Washington, United States, where it is the county seat. The population was 560 at the 2020 census.

Centralia, Washington.title: Centralia, Washington
Centralia, Washington.extract: Centralia () is a city in Lewis County, Washington, United States. It is located along Interstate 5 near the midpoint between Seattle and Portland, Oregon.

Chehalis, Washington.title: Chehalis, Washington
Chehalis, Washington.extract: Chehalis ( shə-HAY-liss) is a city in and the county seat of Lewis County, Washington, United States. The population was 7,439 at the time of the 2020 census.

Chelan, Washington.title: Chelan, Washington
Chelan, Washington.extract: Chelan ( shə-LAN) is a city in Chelan County, Washington, United States. The estimated population was 4,222 at the 2020 census.

Cheney, Washington.title: Cheney, Washington
Cheney, Washington.extract: Cheney ( CHEE-nee) is a city in Spokane County, Washington, United States. The full-time resident population was 13,255 as of the 2020 census.

Chewelah, Washington.title: Chewelah, Washington
Chewelah, Washington.extract: Chewelah ( chə-WEE-lə) is a city in Stevens County, Washington, United States. It is located approximately 45 mi (72 km) northwest of Spokane.

Clarkston, Washington.title: Clarkston, Washington
Clarkston, Washington.extract: Clarkston is a city in Asotin County, Washington, United States. It is part of the Lewiston–Clarkston, ID-WA metropolitan area, and is located west of Lewiston, Idaho, across the Snake River.

Cle Elum, Washington.title: Cle Elum, Washington
Cle Elum, Washington.extract: Cle Elum ( klee EL-əm) is a city in Kittitas County, Washington, United States. The population was 2,157 at the 2020 census.

Clyde Hill, Washington.title: Clyde Hill, Washington
Clyde Hill, Washington.extract: Clyde Hill is a city located in King County, Washington. It is part of the Eastside region, located to the east of Seattle, and is bordered by the cities and towns of Bellevue, Kirkland, Medina, Yarrow Point and Hunts Point.

Colfax, Washington.title: Colfax, Washington
Colfax, Washington.extract: Colfax is a city in and the county seat of Whitman County, Washington, United States. The population was 2,782 at the 2020 census, making Colfax the second largest city in Whitman County behind Pullman.

College Place, Washington.title: College Place, Washington
College Place, Washington.extract: College Place is a city in Walla Walla County, Washington, United States. It neighbors the larger city of Walla Walla, and had a population of 10,090 per Washington State Office of Financial Management (OFM) population estimates.

Colton, Washington.title: Colton, Washington
Colton, Washington.extract: Colton is a town in Whitman County, Washington, United States. The population was 401 at the 2020 census.

Columbia City, Seattle.title: Columbia City, Seattle
Columbia City, Seattle.extract: Columbia City is a neighborhood in southeastern Seattle, Washington, within the city's Rainier Valley district. It has a landmark-protected historic business district and is one of the few Seattle neighborhoods with a long history of ethnic and income diversity.
Columbia City, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in Washington, United States

Colville, Washington.title: Colville, Washington
Colville, Washington.extract: Colville is a city in Stevens County, Washington, United States. The population was 4,917 at the 2020 census, and was estimated at 5,009 in 2024, It is the county seat of Stevens County.

Conconully, Washington.title: Conconully, Washington
Conconully, Washington.extract: Conconully is a town in Okanogan County, Washington, United States. The population was 193 at the 2020 census.

Concrete, Washington.title: Concrete, Washington
Concrete, Washington.extract: Concrete is a town in north-central Skagit County, Washington, United States. It is part of the Mount Vernon-Anacortes, Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area, and had a population of 801 at the 2020 census.

Connell, Washington.title: Connell, Washington
Connell, Washington.extract: Connell () is a city in Franklin County, Washington, United States. The population was 5,441 at the 2020 census, and was estimated at 5,071 in 2024.

Cosmopolis, Washington.title: Cosmopolis, Washington
Cosmopolis, Washington.extract: Cosmopolis is a city in Grays Harbor County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,638 at the 2020 census.

Coulee City, Washington.title: Coulee City, Washington
Coulee City, Washington.extract: Coulee City is a town in Grant County, Washington. The population was 549 at the 2020 census.

Coulee Dam, Washington.title: Coulee Dam, Washington
Coulee Dam, Washington.extract: Coulee Dam is a town in Douglas, Grant, and Okanogan counties in the state of Washington. The Douglas County portion of Coulee Dam is part of the Wenatchee–East Wenatchee Metropolitan Statistical Area.

Coupeville, Washington.title: Coupeville, Washington
Coupeville, Washington.extract: Coupeville is a town on Whidbey Island, in Island County, Washington, United States. It is the county seat of Island County.

Covington, Washington.title: Covington, Washington
Covington, Washington.extract: Covington is a city in King County, Washington, United States. The population was 20,777 at the 2020 census, and was estimated to be 21,567 in 2024.

Creston, Washington.title: Creston, Washington
Creston, Washington.extract: Creston is a town in Lincoln County, Washington, United States. The population was 213 at the 2020 census.

Cusick, Washington.title: Cusick, Washington
Cusick, Washington.extract: Cusick (Salish: čmq̓ʷoqnú ) is a town in Pend Oreille County, Washington, United States. The population was 153 at the 2020 census.
Cusick, Washington.description: Town in Pend Oreille County, Washington, United States

Darrington, Washington.title: Darrington, Washington
Darrington, Washington.extract: Darrington is a town in Snohomish County, Washington, United States. It is located in a North Cascades mountain valley formed by the Sauk and North Fork Stillaguamish rivers.

Davenport, Washington.title: Davenport, Washington
Davenport, Washington.extract: Davenport is the county seat of and the largest city in Lincoln County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,703 at the 2020 census.

Dayton, Washington.title: Dayton, Washington
Dayton, Washington.extract: Dayton is a city in and the county seat of Columbia County, Washington, United States. The population was 2,448 at the 2020 census.

Deer Park, Washington.title: Deer Park, Washington
Deer Park, Washington.extract: Deer Park is a city in Spokane County, Washington, United States. As of the 2020 census, Deer Park had a population of 4,383.

Des Moines, Washington.title: Des Moines, Washington
Des Moines, Washington.extract: Des Moines ( də-MOYNZ) (Lushootseed: baqʷab) is a city in King County, Washington, United States. The population was 32,888 as of the 2020 census.

Diablo, Washington.title: Diablo, Washington
Diablo, Washington.extract: Diablo is an unincorporated community in Whatcom County, Washington, United States. It is located near Diablo Dam in the Ross Lake National Recreation Area, along the Skagit River.

DuPont, Washington.title: DuPont, Washington
DuPont, Washington.extract: DuPont is a city in Pierce County, Washington, United States. The population was 10,151 at the 2020 census.

Duvall, Washington.title: Duvall, Washington
Duvall, Washington.extract: Duvall is a city in King County, Washington, United States, located on SR 203 halfway between Monroe and Carnation. The population was 8,034 at the 2020 census.

East Wenatchee, Washington.title: East Wenatchee, Washington
East Wenatchee, Washington.extract: East Wenatchee is a city in Douglas County, Washington, United States. The population at the 2010 census was 13,190, a 129.1% increase on the 2000 census, having annexed much of the East Wenatchee Bench CDP.

Eatonville, Washington.title: Eatonville, Washington
Eatonville, Washington.extract: Eatonville is a town in Pierce County, Washington, United States. It is 32 mi (51 km) south of Tacoma.

Edgewood, Washington.title: Edgewood, Washington
Edgewood, Washington.extract: Edgewood is a city in Pierce County, Washington, United States. The population was 12,327 at the 2020 census.

Edmonds, Washington.title: Edmonds, Washington
Edmonds, Washington.extract: Edmonds is a city in Snohomish County, Washington, United States. It is located in the southwest corner of the county, facing Puget Sound and the Olympic Mountains to the west.

Electric City, Washington.title: Electric City, Washington
Electric City, Washington.extract: Electric City is a city in Grant County, Washington. The population was 956 at the time of the 2020 census.

Ellensburg, Washington.title: Ellensburg, Washington
Ellensburg, Washington.extract: Ellensburg is a city in and the county seat of Kittitas County, Washington, United States. It is located just east of the Cascade Range near the junction of Interstate 90 and Interstate 82.

Elma, Washington.title: Elma, Washington
Elma, Washington.extract: Elma is a city in Grays Harbor County, Washington, United States. The population was 3,438 at the 2020 census.

Elmer City, Washington.title: Elmer City, Washington
Elmer City, Washington.extract: Elmer City is a town in Okanogan County, Washington, United States. The population was 239 at the 2020 census.

Endicott, Washington.title: Endicott, Washington
Endicott, Washington.extract: Endicott is a town in Whitman County, Washington, United States. The population was 312 at the 2020 census.

Entiat, Washington.title: Entiat, Washington
Entiat, Washington.extract: Entiat is a city in Chelan County, Washington, United States. It is part of the Wenatchee−East Wenatchee Metropolitan Statistical Area.

Enumclaw, Washington.title: Enumclaw, Washington
Enumclaw, Washington.extract: Enumclaw ( EE-nəm-klaw) is a city in King County, Washington, United States. The population was 12,543 at the 2020 census.

Ephrata, Washington.title: Ephrata, Washington
Ephrata, Washington.extract: Ephrata ( ee-FRAY-tə) is a city in and the county seat of Grant County, Washington, United States. Its population was 8,477 at the 2020 census, and was estimated to be 8,718 in 2024.

Ethel, Washington.title: Ethel, Washington
Ethel, Washington.extract: Ethel is an unincorporated community located along U.S. Route 12 in east Lewis County, Washington, United States. It sits between Mary's Corner and Salkum.
Ethel, Washington.description: Unincorporated community in Washington, United States

Everett, Washington.title: Everett, Washington
Everett, Washington.extract: Everett ( EV-rit; Lushootseed: dᶻəɬigʷəd [d͜zəˈɬi̞ɡʷəd]) is the county seat of and the most populous city in Snohomish County, Washington, United States. It is 25 miles (40 km) north of Seattle and is one of the main cities in the metropolitan area and the Puget Sound region.

Everson, Washington.title: Everson, Washington
Everson, Washington.extract: Everson is a city in Whatcom County, Washington, United States. The population was 2,888 at the time of the 2020 census.

Fairfield, Washington.title: Fairfield, Washington
Fairfield, Washington.extract: Fairfield is a town in Spokane County, Washington, United States. The population was 589 at the 2020 census.

Farmington, Washington.title: Farmington, Washington
Farmington, Washington.extract: Farmington is a town in Whitman County, Washington, United States. The population was 131 at the 2020 census.

Federal Way, Washington.title: Federal Way, Washington

Ruston, Washington.extract: Ruston is a city in Pierce County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,055 at the 2020 census.

Sammamish, Washington.title: Sammamish, Washington
Sammamish, Washington.extract: Sammamish ( sə-MAM-ish) is a city in King County, Washington, United States. The population was 67,455 at the 2020 census.

SeaTac, Washington.title: SeaTac, Washington
SeaTac, Washington.extract: SeaTac () is a city in southern King County, Washington, United States. The city is an inner-ring suburb of Seattle and part of the Seattle metropolitan area.

Seattle.title: Seattle
Seattle.extract: Seattle ( see-AT-əl) is the most populous city in the U.S. state of Washington and the Pacific Northwest region of North America.

Sedro-Woolley, Washington.title: Sedro-Woolley, Washington
Sedro-Woolley, Washington.extract: Sedro-Woolley ( SEE-droh WUUL-ee) is a city in Skagit County, Washington, United States. It is part of the Mount Vernon–Anacortes, Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area and had a population of 12,421 at the 2020 census.

Selah, Washington.title: Selah, Washington
Selah, Washington.extract: Selah is a city in Yakima County, Washington, United States. It is north of Yakima and part of its metropolitan area.

Sequim, Washington.title: Sequim, Washington
Sequim, Washington.extract: Sequim ( SKWIM) is a city in Clallam County, Washington, United States. It is located on the north side of the Olympic Peninsula between the Dungeness River and Sequim Bay.

Shelton, Washington.title: Shelton, Washington
Shelton, Washington.extract: Shelton is a city in and the county seat of Mason County, Washington, United States. Shelton is the westernmost city on Puget Sound.

Shoreline, Washington.title: Shoreline, Washington
Shoreline, Washington.extract: Shoreline is a city in King County, Washington, United States. It is located between the city limits of Seattle and the Snohomish County border, approximately 9 miles (14 km) north of Downtown Seattle.

Skykomish, Washington.title: Skykomish, Washington
Skykomish, Washington.extract: Skykomish is a town in King County, Washington, United States. The population was 161 as of the 2020 census, down from an estimated peak of "several thousand" in the 1920s.

Snohomish, Washington.title: Snohomish, Washington
Snohomish, Washington.extract: Snohomish () is a city in Snohomish County, Washington, United States. The population was 10,126 at the 2020 census.

Snoqualmie, Washington.title: Snoqualmie, Washington
Snoqualmie, Washington.extract: Snoqualmie ( snow-KWAWL-mee) is a city next to Snoqualmie Falls in King County, Washington, United States. It is 28 miles (45 km) east of Seattle.

Soap Lake, Washington.title: Soap Lake, Washington
Soap Lake, Washington.extract: Soap Lake is a city in Grant County, Washington, on the shores of Soap Lake. The population was 1,691 at the 2020 census.

South Bend, Washington.title: South Bend, Washington
South Bend, Washington.extract: South Bend is a city in and the county seat of Pacific County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,746 as of the 2020 census.

South Cle Elum, Washington.title: South Cle Elum, Washington
South Cle Elum, Washington.extract: South Cle Elum is a town in Kittitas County, Washington, United States. The population was 559 at the 2020 census.

South Prairie, Washington.title: South Prairie, Washington
South Prairie, Washington.extract: South Prairie is a town in Pierce County, Washington, United States. The population was 373 at the 2020 census.
South Prairie, Washington.description: Town in Pierce County, Washington, United States

Spangle, Washington.title: Spangle, Washington
Spangle, Washington.extract: Spangle is a city in Spokane County, Washington, United States. The population was 280 at the 2020 census.

Spokane, Washington.title: Spokane, Washington
Spokane, Washington.extract: Spokane ( spoh-KAN; Spokane: sƛ̓x̌etkʷ) is a city in and the county seat of Spokane County in the U.S. state of Washington.

Spokane Valley, Washington.title: Spokane Valley, Washington
Spokane Valley, Washington.extract: Spokane Valley is a city in Spokane County, Washington, United States, and the largest suburb of Spokane. It is located east of Spokane, west of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, and surrounds the city of Millwood on three sides.

Sprague, Washington.title: Sprague, Washington
Sprague, Washington.extract: Sprague SPRAYG; is a small city in Lincoln County, Washington, United States. The population was 495 at the 2020 census.

Springdale, Washington.title: Springdale, Washington
Springdale, Washington.extract: Springdale is a town in Stevens County, Washington, United States. The population was 234 at the 2020 census.

St. John, Washington.title: St. John, Washington
St. John, Washington.extract: St. John or Saint John is a town in Whitman County, Washington, United States. The population was 599 at the 2020 census.

Stanwood, Washington.title: Stanwood, Washington
Stanwood, Washington.extract: Stanwood is a city in Snohomish County, Washington, United States. The city is located 50 miles (80 km) north of Seattle, at the mouth of the Stillaguamish River near Camano Island.

Starbuck, Washington.title: Starbuck, Washington
Starbuck, Washington.extract: Starbuck is a town in Columbia County, Washington, United States. The population was 119 at the 2020 census.

Steilacoom, Washington.title: Steilacoom, Washington
Steilacoom, Washington.extract: Steilacoom ( STIL-ə-kəm) is a town in Pierce County, Washington, United States. The population was 6,727 at the 2020 census.

Stevenson, Washington.title: Stevenson, Washington
Stevenson, Washington.extract: Stevenson is a city along the Columbia River in Skamania County, Washington, United States. It is the county seat of Skamania County and part of the Portland metropolitan area.

Sultan, Washington.title: Sultan, Washington
Sultan, Washington.extract: Sultan is a city in Snohomish County, Washington, United States. It is located approximately 23 miles (37 km) east of Everett at the confluence of the Skykomish River and the Sultan River, a minor tributary.

Sumas, Washington.title: Sumas, Washington
Sumas, Washington.extract: Sumas (SOO-mas) is a city in Whatcom County, Washington, United States. It had a population of 1,583 as of the 2020 census.

Sumner, Washington.title: Sumner, Washington
Sumner, Washington.extract: Sumner is a city in northern Pierce County, Washington, United States. The population was 10,621 at the 2020 census.

Sunnyside, Washington.title: Sunnyside, Washington
Sunnyside, Washington.extract: Sunnyside is a city in Yakima County, Washington, United States. The population was 16,375 at the 2020 census, making it the second-most populous city in Yakima County.

Tacoma, Washington.title: Tacoma, Washington
Tacoma, Washington.extract: Tacoma ( tə-KOH-mə) is a city in and the county seat of Pierce County, Washington, United States. A port city, it is situated along Puget Sound roughly 30 miles (48 km) from Seattle and Olympia, and 58 miles (93 km) northwest of Mount Rainier National Park.

Tekoa, Washington.title: Tekoa, Washington
Tekoa, Washington.extract: Tekoa ( TEE-koh) is a rural city in Whitman County, Washington, United States. The population was 817 at the 2020 census.

Tenino, Washington.title: Tenino, Washington
Tenino, Washington.extract: Tenino () is a city in Thurston County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,870 at the 2020 census.

Tieton, Washington.title: Tieton, Washington
Tieton, Washington.extract: Tieton () is a city in Yakima County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,389 at the 2020 census.

Toledo, Washington.title: Toledo, Washington
Toledo, Washington.extract: Toledo is a city in Lewis County, Washington, United States. The community is situated on the Cowlitz River.

Tonasket, Washington.title: Tonasket, Washington
Tonasket, Washington.extract: Tonasket is a city in Okanogan County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,103 at the 2020 census.

Toppenish, Washington.title: Toppenish, Washington
Toppenish, Washington.extract: Toppenish () is a city in Yakima County, Washington, United States. The population was 8,854 at the 2020 census.

Tukwila, Washington.title: Tukwila, Washington
Tukwila, Washington.extract: Tukwila ( tuk-WIL-ə) is a suburban city in King County, Washington, United States, located immediately to the south of Seattle. The population was 21,798 at the 2020 census.

Tumwater, Washington.title: Tumwater, Washington
Tumwater, Washington.extract: Tumwater is a city in Thurston County, Washington, United States. The population was 25,350 at the 2020 census.

Twisp, Washington.title: Twisp, Washington
Twisp, Washington.extract: Twisp is a town in Okanogan County in north central Washington, which sits at the confluence of the Twisp and Methow rivers. The population was 919 at the time of the 2010 census and increased to 992 at the time of the 2020 census.

Union Gap, Washington.title: Union Gap, Washington
Union Gap, Washington.extract: Union Gap is a city in Yakima County, Washington, United States. The population was 6,568 at the 2020 census.

Uniontown, Washington.title: Uniontown, Washington
Uniontown, Washington.extract: Uniontown is a town in Whitman County, Washington, United States. The population was 389 at the 2020 census.

University Place, Washington.title: University Place, Washington
University Place, Washington.extract: University Place is a city in Pierce County, Washington, United States. Its population was 34,866 at the 2020 census.

Vader, Washington.title: Vader, Washington
Vader, Washington.extract: Vader is a city in Lewis County, Washington, United States. The community began in the 1870s and was known under several different names during its early years.
Vader, Washington.description: City in Lewis County, Washington state

Vancouver, Washington.title: Vancouver, Washington
Vancouver, Washington.extract: Vancouver ( van-KOO-vər) is a city in Clark County, Washington, United States, located on the north bank of the Columbia River. It had a population of 190,915 at the 2020 census, making it the fourth-most populous city in Washington.

Waitsburg, Washington.title: Waitsburg, Washington
Waitsburg, Washington.extract: Waitsburg is a city in Walla Walla County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,166 at the 2020 census.

Walla Walla, Washington.title: Walla Walla, Washington
Walla Walla, Washington.extract: Walla Walla ( WAH-lə WAH-lə) is a city in and the county seat of Walla Walla County, Washington, United States. It is one of the largest cities in Southeastern Washington with a population of 34,060 at the 2020 census, estimated to have decreased to 33,339 as of 2023.

Wapato, Washington.title: Wapato, Washington
Wapato, Washington.extract: Wapato () is a town in Yakima County, Washington, United States. The population was 4,607 at the 2020 census.

Warden, Washington.title: Warden, Washington
Warden, Washington.extract: Warden is a city in Grant County, Washington, United States. The population was 2,449 at the 2020 census.

Washougal, Washington.title: Washougal, Washington
Washougal, Washington.extract: Washougal ( wah-SHOO-gəl) is a city in Clark County, Washington, United States. The population was 17,039 as of the 2020 census.

Washtucna, Washington.title: Washtucna, Washington
Washtucna, Washington.extract: Washtucna () is a town in Adams County, Washington, United States. The population was 211 at the 2020 census, a 1% increase over the previous census.

Waterville, Washington.title: Waterville, Washington
Waterville, Washington.extract: Waterville is a town in and the county seat of Douglas County, Washington, United States. As a part of Douglas County, it is part of the Wenatchee-East Wenatchee metropolitan area.

Waverly, Washington.title: Waverly, Washington
Waverly, Washington.extract: Waverly is a town in Spokane County, Washington, United States. The population was 121 at the 2020 census.

Wenatchee, Washington.title: Wenatchee, Washington
Wenatchee, Washington.extract: Wenatchee ( wen-ACH-ee) is the county seat of and the most populous city in Chelan County, Washington, United States. The population was 35,508 as of the 2020 census.

West Richland, Washington.title: West Richland, Washington
West Richland, Washington.extract: West Richland is a city in Benton County, Washington. The population was 16,295 at the time of the 2020 census.

Westport, Washington.title: Westport, Washington
Westport, Washington.extract: Westport is a city in Grays Harbor County, Washington, United States. It had a population of 2,213 at the 2020 census.

White Salmon, Washington.title: White Salmon, Washington
White Salmon, Washington.extract: White Salmon is a city in Klickitat County, Washington, United States. It is located in the Columbia River Gorge.

Wilbur, Washington.title: Wilbur, Washington
Wilbur, Washington.extract: Wilbur is a town in Lincoln County, Washington, United States. The population was 895 at the 2020 census.

Wilkeson, Washington.title: Wilkeson, Washington
Wilkeson, Washington.extract: Wilkeson is a town in Pierce County, Washington, United States. The population was 499 at the 2020 census.

Wilson Creek, Washington.title: Wilson Creek, Washington
Wilson Creek, Washington.extract: Wilson Creek is a town in Grant County, Washington, United States. The population was 204 at the 2020 census.

Winlock, Washington.title: Winlock, Washington
Winlock, Washington.extract: Winlock () is a city in Lewis County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,472 at the 2020 census, and was estimated to be 2,515 in 2024.

Winthrop, Washington.title: Winthrop, Washington
Winthrop, Washington.extract: Winthrop is a town in Okanogan County, Washington, United States. It is located on the North Cascades Highway, east of Mazama and north of Twisp.

Woodinville, Washington.title: Woodinville, Washington
Woodinville, Washington.extract: Woodinville is a city in King County, Washington, United States. The population was 13,069 at the 2020 census.

Woodland, Washington.title: Woodland, Washington
Woodland, Washington.extract: Woodland is a city in Clark and Cowlitz counties in Washington, United States. Most residents live within Cowlitz County, in which the majority of the city lies.

Woodway, Washington.title: Woodway, Washington
Woodway, Washington.extract: Woodway is a city in Snohomish County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,318 at the 2020 census.

Yacolt, Washington.title: Yacolt, Washington
Yacolt, Washington.extract: Yacolt is a town in Clark County, Washington, United States. The 2023 population is estimated to be 1,626.

Yakima, Washington.title: Yakima, Washington
Yakima, Washington.extract: Yakima ( or ) is a city in and the county seat of Yakima County, Washington, United States, and the state's 11th most populous city. As of the 2020 census, the city had a total population of 96,968 and a metropolitan population of 256,728.

Yarrow Point, Washington.title: Yarrow Point, Washington
Yarrow Point, Washington.extract: Yarrow Point is a town in King County, Washington, United States. The population was 1,134 at the 2020 census.

Yelm, Washington.title: Yelm, Washington
Yelm, Washington.extract: Yelm () is a city in Thurston County, Washington, United States bordering Pierce County along the Nisqually River. Its population was 10,617 at the 2020 census.

Zillah, Washington.title: Zillah, Washington
Zillah, Washington.extract: Zillah is a city in Yakima County, Washington, United States, with a population of 3,179 as of the 2020 census.

Lower Queen Anne, Seattle.title: Lower Queen Anne, Seattle
Lower Queen Anne, Seattle.extract: Lower Queen Anne is a neighborhood in northwestern Seattle, Washington, at the base of Queen Anne Hill. While its boundaries are not precise, the toponym usually refers to the shopping, office, and residential districts to the north and west of Seattle Center.

Queen Anne, Seattle.title: Queen Anne, Seattle
Queen Anne, Seattle.extract: Queen Anne is a neighborhood in northwestern Seattle, Washington. Queen Anne covers an area of 2.8 square miles (7.3 km2), and has a population of about 34,000.

Capitol Hill, Seattle.title: Capitol Hill, Seattle
Capitol Hill, Seattle.extract: Capitol Hill is a densely populated residential district and a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States. It is immediately east of Downtown Seattle and north of First Hill.
Capitol Hill, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States

Ballard, Seattle.title: Ballard, Seattle
Ballard, Seattle.extract: Ballard is a neighborhood in northwestern Seattle, Washington, United States.

Fremont, Seattle.title: Fremont, Seattle
Fremont, Seattle.extract: Fremont is a neighborhood in northern Seattle, Washington, United States. Originally a separate city, it was annexed to Seattle in 1891.
Fremont, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in Washington, United States

Wallingford, Seattle.title: Wallingford, Seattle
Wallingford, Seattle.extract: Wallingford is a neighborhood in north central Seattle, lying on a hill above the north shore of Lake Union about four miles from the downtown core. The neighborhood developed quickly during the early 20th century after the establishment of the University of Washington to the east.

University District, Seattle.title: University District, Seattle
University District, Seattle.extract: The University District (commonly the U District) is a neighborhood and a major district in central northeastern Seattle, Washington, comprising several distinct neighborhoods.

Georgetown, Seattle.title: Georgetown, Seattle
Georgetown, Seattle.extract: Georgetown is a neighborhood in southern Seattle, Washington, United States.

Beacon Hill, Seattle.title: Beacon Hill, Seattle
Beacon Hill, Seattle.extract: Beacon Hill is a hill and neighborhood in southeastern Seattle, Washington. It is roughly bounded on the west by Interstate 5, on the north by Interstate 90, on the east by Rainier Avenue South, Cheasty Boulevard South, and Martin Luther King Junior Way South, and on the south by the Seattle city boundary.
Beacon Hill, Seattle.description: Seattle neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Rainier Valley, Seattle.title: Rainier Valley, Seattle
Rainier Valley, Seattle.extract: Rainier Valley ( ray-NEER) is a neighborhood in southeastern Seattle, Washington. It is located north of Rainier Beach, south of the Central District, east of Beacon Hill, and west of Mount Baker, Seward Park, and Leschi.

West Seattle.title: West Seattle
West Seattle.extract: West Seattle is a conglomeration of neighborhoods in Seattle, Washington, United States. It comprises two of the thirteen districts, Delridge and Southwest, and encompasses all of Seattle west of the Duwamish River.
West Seattle.description: Neighborhood between the Duwamish River and Puget Sound

Pioneer Square, Seattle.title: Pioneer Square, Seattle
Pioneer Square, Seattle.extract: Pioneer Square is a neighborhood in the southwest corner of downtown Seattle, Washington, US. It was once the heart of the city: Seattle's founders settled there in 1852, following a brief six-month settlement at Alki Point on the far side of Elliott Bay.

Belltown, Seattle.title: Belltown, Seattle
Belltown, Seattle.extract: Belltown is the most densely populated neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States, located on the city's downtown waterfront on land that was artificially flattened as part of a regrading project.
Belltown, Seattle.description: Most densely populated neighborhood in Seattle, Washington

South Lake Union, Seattle.title: South Lake Union, Seattle
South Lake Union, Seattle.extract: South Lake Union (sometimes SLU) (Lushootseed: čaʔkʷšəd) is a neighborhood in central Seattle, Washington, so named because it is at the southern tip of Lake Union.

Downtown Seattle.title: Downtown Seattle
Downtown Seattle.extract: Downtown is the central business district of Seattle, Washington. It is fairly compact compared with other city centers on the U.S. West Coast due to its geographical situation, being hemmed in on the north and east by hills, on the west by Elliott Bay, and on the south by reclaimed land that was once tidal flats.
Downtown Seattle.description: Central business district of Seattle, Washington, U.S.

Chinatown–International District, Seattl.title: Chinatown–International District, Seattle
Chinatown–International District, Seattl.extract: The Chinatown–International District (abbreviated as CID) is a neighborhood of Seattle, Washington. It is the center of the city's Asian American community.
Chinatown–International District, Seattl.description: Historic district in Washington, United States

Central District, Seattle.title: Central District, Seattle
Central District, Seattle.extract: The Central District (commonly called the Central Area or The CD) is a mostly residential neighborhood in Seattle located east of downtown and First Hill (12th Avenue and Rainier Avenue); west of Madrona, Leschi and Mt. Baker neighborhoods; south of Capitol Hill, and north of Rainier Valley.

Magnolia, Seattle.title: Magnolia, Seattle
Magnolia, Seattle.extract: Magnolia is the second largest neighborhood of Seattle, Washington, by area, located northwest of downtown. It occupies a hilly headland overlooking Puget Sound.
Magnolia, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States

Greenwood, Seattle.title: Greenwood, Seattle
Greenwood, Seattle.extract: Greenwood is a neighborhood in north central Seattle, Washington, United States. The intersection of Greenwood Avenue North and North 85th Street is the commercial center.
Greenwood, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Green Lake, Seattle.title: Green Lake, Seattle
Green Lake, Seattle.extract: Green Lake is a neighborhood in north central Seattle, Washington. Its centerpiece is the lake and park after which it is named.

Northgate, Seattle.title: Northgate, Seattle
Northgate, Seattle.extract: Northgate is a neighborhood in north Seattle, Washington, named for and surrounding Northgate Mall, the first covered mall in the United States. Its north-south principal arterials are Roosevelt Way NE and Aurora Avenue N (SR 99), and its east-west principal arterials are NE Northgate Way and 130th Street.
Northgate, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Lake City, Seattle.title: Lake City, Seattle
Lake City, Seattle.extract: Lake City is a neighborhood in the northeast region of Seattle, centered along Lake City Way NE (SR-522), 7–8 miles (11–13 km) northeast of downtown Seattle.
Lake City, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Wedgwood, Seattle.title: Wedgwood, Seattle
Wedgwood, Seattle.extract: Wedgwood is a middle-class residential neighborhood of northeast Seattle, Washington with a modest commercial strip. Wedgwood is located about two miles (3.2 km) north, and slightly east, of the University of Washington; it is about six miles (9.7 km) northeast of Downtown.

Ravenna, Seattle.title: Ravenna, Seattle
Ravenna, Seattle.extract: Ravenna is a neighborhood in northeastern Seattle, Washington named after Ravenna, Italy. Though Ravenna is considered a residential neighborhood, it also is home to several businesses, many of which are located in the University Village, a shopping mall.

Madison Park, Seattle.title: Madison Park, Seattle
Madison Park, Seattle.extract: Madison Park is a neighborhood in eastern Seattle, Washington, United States. It is named after the city park at the foot of Madison Street on the Lake Washington shore.

Madrona, Seattle.title: Madrona, Seattle
Madrona, Seattle.extract: Madrona is a mostly residential neighborhood in east Seattle, Washington.
Madrona, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Leschi, Seattle.title: Leschi, Seattle
Leschi, Seattle.extract: Leschi is a neighborhood in the city of Seattle, Washington, United States. Located on the western shore of Lake Washington, the residential neighborhood was named by its 19th-century developer for Chief Leschi of the Nisqually tribe, who was executed by territorial authorities in 1858 in Pierce County, Washington.
Leschi, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Mount Baker, Seattle.title: Mount Baker, Seattle
Mount Baker, Seattle.extract: Mount Baker is a neighborhood in southeastern Seattle, Washington. The neighborhood's name comes from the view of Mount Baker in Whatcom County, that is seen by looking north over Lake Washington.
Mount Baker, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in Washington, United States

Phinney Ridge, Seattle.title: Phinney Ridge, Seattle
Phinney Ridge, Seattle.extract: Phinney Ridge is a neighborhood in north central Seattle, Washington, United States. It is named after the ridge which runs north and south, separating Ballard from Green Lake, from approximately N. 45th to N. 70th Street.
Phinney Ridge, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Bitter Lake, Seattle.title: Bitter Lake, Seattle
Bitter Lake, Seattle.extract: Bitter Lake is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States, named after its most notable feature, Bitter Lake. It was a mostly natural forest of Douglas-fir and Western Redcedar, inhabited by Native Americans, until the late 19th century.
Bitter Lake, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States

Broadview, Seattle.title: Broadview, Seattle
Broadview, Seattle.extract: Broadview is a neighborhood in northwestern Seattle, Washington, United States. It is at the northwestern corner of the city, adjacent to Puget Sound and the city of Shoreline to the north.
Broadview, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Crown Hill, Seattle.title: Crown Hill, Seattle
Crown Hill, Seattle.extract: Crown Hill is a neighborhood in the city of Seattle, Washington, United States.
Crown Hill, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States

Laurelhurst, Seattle.title: Laurelhurst, Seattle
Laurelhurst, Seattle.extract: Laurelhurst is a residential neighborhood in northeastern Seattle, Washington, US.

Montlake, Seattle.title: Montlake, Seattle
Montlake, Seattle.extract: Montlake is a wealthy residential neighborhood in central Seattle, Washington. It is located along the Montlake Cut of the Lake Washington Ship Canal, bounded to the north by Portage Bay, to the east by the Washington Park Arboretum, and to the south and west by Interlaken Park.
Montlake, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Eastlake, Seattle.title: Eastlake, Seattle
Eastlake, Seattle.extract: Eastlake is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, so named because of its location on the eastern shore of Lake Union.
Eastlake, Seattle.description: Neighborhood of Seattle in Washington, United States

Interbay, Seattle.title: Interbay, Seattle
Interbay, Seattle.extract: Interbay is a neighborhood in northwestern Seattle, Washington. It consists of the valley between Queen Anne Hill on the east and Magnolia on the west, plus filled-in areas of Smith Cove and Salmon Bay.

Delridge, Seattle.title: Delridge, Seattle
Delridge, Seattle.extract: Delridge is a district in Seattle, Washington, United States that stretches along Delridge Way, an arterial that follows the eastern slope of the valley of Longfellow Creek, from near its source just within the southern city limits north to the West Seattle Bridge over the Duwamish River.

Alki, Seattle.title: Alki Point, Seattle
Alki, Seattle.extract: Alki Point (, Lushootseed: sbaqʷabqs, lit. 'prairie point') is a neighborhood in western Seattle, Washington. It is a point jutting into Puget Sound, the westernmost landform in the city's West Seattle district.
Alki, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in Washington, United States

High Point, Seattle.title: West Seattle
High Point, Seattle.extract: West Seattle is a conglomeration of neighborhoods in Seattle, Washington, United States. It comprises two of the thirteen districts, Delridge and Southwest, and encompasses all of Seattle west of the Duwamish River.
High Point, Seattle.description: Neighborhood between the Duwamish River and Puget Sound

South Park, Seattle.title: South Park, Seattle
South Park, Seattle.extract: South Park is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington. It is located just south of Georgetown across the Duwamish River, and just north of the city of Tukwila.

Sand Point, Seattle.title: Sand Point, Seattle
Sand Point, Seattle.extract: Sand Point is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States, named after and consisting mostly of the Sand Point peninsula that juts into Lake Washington, which is itself largely given over to Magnuson Park.

View Ridge, Seattle.title: View Ridge, Seattle
View Ridge, Seattle.extract: View Ridge is a neighborhood in north Seattle, Washington. As with all Seattle neighborhoods, its boundaries are not fixed, but can be thought of as NE 65th Street in the south, 40th and 45th Avenues NE in the west, the Sand Point Country Club in the north, and Sand Point Way NE in the east.
View Ridge, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Maple Leaf, Seattle.title: Maple Leaf, Seattle
Maple Leaf, Seattle.extract: Maple Leaf is a mostly residential neighborhood located in northeast Seattle.
Maple Leaf, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Roosevelt, Seattle.title: Roosevelt, Seattle
Roosevelt, Seattle.extract: Roosevelt is a neighborhood in northern Seattle, Washington. Its main thoroughfare, originally 10th Avenue, was renamed Roosevelt Way upon Theodore Roosevelt's death in 1919.
Roosevelt, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Haller Lake, Seattle.title: Haller Lake, Seattle
Haller Lake, Seattle.extract: Haller Lake (Lushootseed: sisaɬtəb) is a small lake and neighborhood in north central Seattle, Washington, named for Theodore N. Haller, who platted the neighborhood in 1905. His father, Granville O. Haller, was one of Seattle's early settlers, an army officer who amassed a large estate in the region.
Haller Lake, Seattle.description: Lake and neighborhood in Seattle, Washington

Licton Springs, Seattle.title: Licton Springs, Seattle
Licton Springs, Seattle.extract: Licton Springs or North College Park is a neighborhood in the informal Northgate district of North Seattle.
Licton Springs, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Victory Heights, Seattle.title: Victory Heights, Seattle
Victory Heights, Seattle.extract: Victory Heights is a neighborhood in the Lake City district of Seattle, Washington. Victory Heights was named after the Victory Highway, which formed the eastern border of the area.

Matthews Beach, Seattle.title: Matthews Beach, Seattle
Matthews Beach, Seattle.extract: Matthews Beach is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington; it and Meadowbrook are the southern neighborhoods of the annexed township of Lake City (1954). Matthews Beach lies about 2 miles (3.2 km) northeast of the University of Washington, about 8 miles (13 km) northeast of Downtown.
Matthews Beach, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Hawthorne Hills, Seattle.title: Hawthorne Hills, Seattle
Hawthorne Hills, Seattle.extract: Hawthorne Hills is a residential neighborhood in Seattle, Washington. It is officially split between the neighborhoods of Bryant and Windermere, but is generally recognized as a distinct neighborhood.

Bryant, Seattle.title: Bryant, Seattle
Bryant, Seattle.extract: Bryant is a residential neighborhood in northeastern Seattle, Washington.
Bryant, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Windermere, Seattle.title: Windermere, Seattle
Windermere, Seattle.extract: Windermere is a residential neighborhood in northeastern Seattle, Washington, named after Windermere in England's Lake District.

Cedar Park, Seattle.title: Cedar Park, Seattle
Cedar Park, Seattle.extract: Cedar Park is a neighborhood in the Lake City district of Seattle, Washington. The name generally refers to the residential neighborhoods east of Lake City adjoining Lake Washington.
Cedar Park, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States

Meadowbrook, Seattle.title: Meadowbrook, Seattle
Meadowbrook, Seattle.extract: Meadowbrook is a neighborhood in the Lake City district (township annexed in 1954) of Seattle, Washington. Meadowbrook is centered on open fields adjacent to the Community Center, Meadowbrook swimming pool, and Nathan Hale High School.
Meadowbrook, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Olympic Hills, Seattle.title: Olympic Hills, Seattle
Olympic Hills, Seattle.extract: Olympic Hills is a neighborhood in the Lake City district of Seattle, Washington. The architecture is very diverse, ranging from homes displaced from the Interstate 5 construction, to newer construction.
Olympic Hills, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States

Pinehurst, Seattle.title: Pinehurst, Seattle
Pinehurst, Seattle.extract: Pinehurst is a neighborhood in the Northgate area of Seattle, Washington, United States. It is bounded by NE 145th Street to the north, NE Northgate Way to the south, I-5 to the west, and Lake City Way to the east.

First Hill, Seattle.title: First Hill, Seattle
First Hill, Seattle.extract: First Hill is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States. It is named for the hill on which it is located, which in turn is so named for being the first hill encountered while traveling east from downtown Seattle toward Lake Washington.

Yesler Terrace, Seattle.title: Yesler Terrace, Seattle
Yesler Terrace, Seattle.extract: Yesler Terrace is a 22-acre (9 ha) mixed-income, mixed-use neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States. It was originally completed in 1941 as the state's first public housing development and the first racially integrated public housing development in the United States.

Judkins Park, Seattle.title: Atlantic, Seattle
Judkins Park, Seattle.extract: Atlantic is a neighborhood in the Central District of Seattle, Washington, United States. It is the northernmost neighborhood in the Rainier Valley area, located between Mount Baker Ridge and Beacon Hill, and may also be considered part of South Seattle.

Atlantic, Seattle.title: Atlantic, Seattle
Atlantic, Seattle.extract: Atlantic is a neighborhood in the Central District of Seattle, Washington, United States. It is the northernmost neighborhood in the Rainier Valley area, located between Mount Baker Ridge and Beacon Hill, and may also be considered part of South Seattle.

Seward Park, Seattle.title: Seward Park, Seattle
Seward Park, Seattle.extract: Seward Park is a neighborhood in southeastern Seattle, Washington, just west of Seward Park. It is part of Seattle's South End.

Brighton, Seattle.title: Brighton, Seattle
Brighton, Seattle.extract: Brighton is a primarily residential neighborhood in southern Seattle, Washington, part of the greater Rainier Valley district and centered about a mile and a half south of the Columbia City neighborhood.

Dunlap, Seattle.title: Dunlap, Seattle
Dunlap, Seattle.extract: Dunlap is a neighborhood in southern Seattle, Washington, just north of Rainier Beach. It is home to Dunlap Elementary School, part of the Seattle Public Schools.

Rainier Beach, Seattle.title: Rainier Beach, Seattle
Rainier Beach, Seattle.extract: Rainier Beach ( ray-NEER) is a set of neighborhoods in Seattle, Washington, that are mostly residential. Also called Atlantic City, Rainier Beach can include Dunlap, Pritchard Island, and Rainier View neighborhoods.

Hillman City, Seattle.title: Hillman City, Seattle
Hillman City, Seattle.extract: Hillman City is a primarily residential neighborhood in southeastern Seattle, Washington, located in the Rainier Valley and centered about a half mile south of the Columbia City neighborhood. It was annexed by Seattle in January 1907, along with the rest of the town of Southeast Seattle.

Genesee, Seattle.title: Genesee, Seattle
Genesee, Seattle.extract: Genesee is a neighborhood of West Seattle in Seattle, Washington. It extends north from SW Genesee St. to SW Charlestown St., and west from 46th to 56th Avenues SW.

Fauntleroy, Seattle.title: Fauntleroy, Seattle
Fauntleroy, Seattle.extract: Fauntleroy is a neighborhood in the southwest corner of Seattle, Washington. Part of West Seattle and situated on Puget Sound's Fauntleroy Cove (into which Fauntleroy Creek flows from its source in Fauntleroy Park), it faces Vashon Island, Blake Island, and the Kitsap Peninsula to the west.
Fauntleroy, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Arbor Heights, Seattle.title: Arbor Heights, Seattle
Arbor Heights, Seattle.extract: Arbor Heights is a neighborhood of West Seattle in Seattle, Washington, made up of the area south of SW Roxbury Street, north and east of Puget Sound, but excluding the downhill portion on the west side of this region. It is the southernmost section of West Seattle.

Roxhill, Seattle.title: Delridge, Seattle
Roxhill, Seattle.extract: Delridge is a district in Seattle, Washington, United States that stretches along Delridge Way, an arterial that follows the eastern slope of the valley of Longfellow Creek, from near its source just within the southern city limits north to the West Seattle Bridge over the Duwamish River.

Industrial District, Seattle.title: Industrial District, Seattle
Industrial District, Seattle.extract: The Industrial District is a neighborhood and the principal industrial area of Seattle, Washington.

SoDo, Seattle.title: SoDo, Seattle
SoDo, Seattle.extract: SoDo (alternatively SODO) is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, that makes up part of the city's Industrial District.
SoDo, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States

Harbor Island, Seattle.title: Harbor Island, Seattle
Harbor Island, Seattle.extract: Harbor Island is an artificial island in the mouth of the Duwamish River in Seattle, Washington, United States, where it empties into Elliott Bay. Built by the Puget Sound Bridge and Dredging Company, it was completed in 1909 and was then the largest artificial island in the world, at 350 acres (1.4 km2).

Westlake, Seattle.title: Westlake, Seattle
Westlake, Seattle.extract: Westlake is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington. It was named after its location on the western shore of Lake Union.

Denny Triangle, Seattle.title: Denny Triangle, Seattle
Denny Triangle, Seattle.extract: The Denny Triangle is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States, that stretches north of Downtown Seattle to the grounds of the Seattle Center.

Denny Regrade, Seattle.extract: The Denny Triangle is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States, that stretches north of Downtown Seattle to the grounds of the Seattle Center.

Loyal Heights, Seattle.title: Loyal Heights, Seattle
Loyal Heights, Seattle.extract: Loyal Heights is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington. It is considered part of greater Ballard.

Whittier Heights, Seattle.title: Whittier Heights, Seattle
Whittier Heights, Seattle.extract: Whittier Heights is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington. It is considered part of greater Ballard.

West Woodland, Seattle.title: West Woodland, Seattle
West Woodland, Seattle.extract: West Woodland is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington. The city's Department of Neighborhoods places West Woodland in the south east corner of Ballard.

Sunset Hill, Seattle.title: Sunset Hill, Seattle
Sunset Hill, Seattle.extract: Sunset Hill is an area located in the northwest corner of the Ballard neighborhood of Seattle, Washington. It is home to the Sunset Hill Community Association.

Madison Valley, Seattle.title: Madison Valley, Seattle
Madison Valley, Seattle.extract: Madison Valley is a neighborhood in Seattle located east of Capitol Hill; west of Washington Park; south of Montlake; and north of Madrona.

Denny-Blaine, Seattle.title: Denny-Blaine, Seattle
Denny-Blaine, Seattle.extract: Denny-Blaine (also known as Harrison) is a neighborhood in east central Seattle, Washington.

Broadway, Seattle.title: Broadway (Seattle)
Broadway, Seattle.extract: Broadway is a major north–south thoroughfare in Seattle, Washington. The 1.6-mile-long (2.6 km) arterial runs north from Yesler Way at Yesler Terrace through the First Hill and Capitol Hill neighborhoods to East Roy Street.

Lawton Park, Seattle.title: Magnolia, Seattle
Lawton Park, Seattle.extract: Magnolia is the second largest neighborhood of Seattle, Washington, by area, located northwest of downtown. It occupies a hilly headland overlooking Puget Sound.
Lawton Park, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States

Briarcliff, Seattle.title: Briarcliff, Seattle
Briarcliff, Seattle.extract: Briarcliff is a neighborhood in Seattle, Washington. The city's Department of Neighborhoods places Briarcliff on the west side of Magnolia, south of Discovery Park.

Southeast Magnolia, Seattle.title: Magnolia, Seattle
Southeast Magnolia, Seattle.extract: Magnolia is the second largest neighborhood of Seattle, Washington, by area, located northwest of downtown. It occupies a hilly headland overlooking Puget Sound.

Fairmount Park, Seattle.title: Fairmount Park, Seattle
Fairmount Park, Seattle.extract: The Fairmount Park is a neighborhood of West Seattle in Seattle, Washington. It runs southwest along both sides of Fauntleroy Way, from SW Graham Street in the south to SW Edmunds Street in the north.
Fairmount Park, Seattle.description: Neighborhood in Seattle, Washington, United States

Gatewood, Seattle.title: Gatewood, Seattle
Gatewood, Seattle.extract: Gatewood is a neighborhood of West Seattle in Seattle, Washington. Situated on the highest hill in Seattle it overlooks Puget Sound, the Olympic Mountains, and downtown Seattle.
Gatewood, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Seaview, Seattle.title: Seaview, Seattle
Seaview, Seattle.extract: Seaview is a neighborhood in West Seattle, Washington. Seaview is bordered by Puget Sound to the west, the Alki and Genesee neighborhoods to the north, Fairmount Park to the east, and Gatewood to the south.

North Admiral, Seattle.title: North Admiral, Seattle
North Admiral, Seattle.extract: North Admiral (locally known as Admiral or Admiral District) is the oldest neighborhood in West Seattle, Washington. In the early 1900s, it was connected to Seattle by ferries and a cable car.

Holly Park, Seattle.title: NewHolly, Seattle
Holly Park, Seattle.extract: NewHolly (formerly Holly Park) is a neighborhood in southeastern Seattle, Washington, United States. It is part of Seattle's South End.

North College Park, Seattle.title: Licton Springs, Seattle
North College Park, Seattle.extract: Licton Springs or North College Park is a neighborhood in the informal Northgate district of North Seattle.
North College Park, Seattle.description: Seattle Neighborhood in King, Washington, United States

Wedgewood, Seattle.title: Wedgwood, Seattle
Wedgewood, Seattle.extract: Wedgwood is a middle-class residential neighborhood of northeast Seattle, Washington with a modest commercial strip. Wedgwood is located about two miles (3.2 km) north, and slightly east, of the University of Washington; it is about six miles (9.7 km) northeast of Downtown.
